name: Archify
hook: Agent skill that turns any idea, plan, or codebase into beautiful interactive diagrams — architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, and lifecycle — output as self-contained HTML with motion, dark/light themes, and PNG/SVG/WebM export. Local deterministic validation (typed JSON IR with constraint checks) means Claude can verify the diagram is structurally correct before showing it to you. Reads Mermaid as input, authors a fresh Archify diagram instead of copying its styling. 77.1k stars; install is one command.

name: UI/UX Pro Max Skill
hook: v2.0's Design System Generator analyzes project requirements and produces a complete tailored design system in seconds — 192 industry-specific reasoning rules, 79 searchable UI styles, 192 color palettes, 74 font pairings, 25 chart types, 16 tech stacks. 131.9k stars on GitHub, 347k+ installs in the Skillselion catalog. Chase AI dedicated a full video to the v2.0 upgrade, calling it the must-have design skill.

name: Claude Code Projects (Redesigned Beta)
hook: Anthropic redesigned Claude Code Projects from a folder system into a coordinator-driven platform: describe a goal, and a coordinator agent scopes it, spawns parallel agent threads each with their own cloud session and branch, monitors progress, and assembles the result. A shared Project Library collects files and artifacts from all threads. Cloud sessions keep running after you close your laptop. Beta is rolling out to Claude Pro and Max users in cloud sessions this week.

name: "You Should Know" Built-in Mod
hook: Shipped in v2.1.287 alongside Claude Mods: a built-in side agent that watches your session in parallel and proactively flags things you or Claude might overlook — missed edge cases, risks in the proposed change, context that got dropped. Off by default; enable with `/plugin enable cc-plugin-you-should-know@builtin` in first-party sessions with telemetry on. The first official Anthropic-authored mod demonstrating what the Mods platform enables.

name: Ponytail
hook: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. Ships a six-step YAGNI decision ladder that fires before every code change: does this need to exist, is it already in the codebase, standard library, platform, or installed deps, can it be one line? Only then: write minimum viable. Six slash commands, support for 10+ agents including Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor. JetBrains benchmarked 15% output reduction across 80 tasks; Chase AI's testing showed up to 50% code cuts and 53% Opus cost drop. 150.1k stars.

name: Caveman
hook: why use many token when few token do trick. A skill + proxy for 30+ coding agents that forces responses into compressed caveman-speak while preserving code, commands, and exact error messages verbatim. Started as a Friday joke in April 2026, hit #1 on Hacker News with 904 points and 366 comments, #8 Product of the Day on Product Hunt, and now sits at 109k stars. JetBrains tested 86 real Claude Code tasks: 8.5% fewer output tokens with no detectable quality change.

name: coucou
hook: A tiny friend that lives in your Mac's notch — or at the top of your screen on Windows/Linux — watching your Claude Code sessions. See every read, edit, and run step by step; permission requests show up with Allow/Deny buttons for one-click approval from the notch; built-in chat without switching windows. v0.1.6 ships Mochi on the desktop (pet-mode overlay); integrations for Stripe, GitHub, Vercel, n8n, Notion, and Cal.com each get a colored Mochi. macOS 15+ (Swift 6) and Windows 10/11 (Tauri 2). 3.3k stars, up from 3.1k yesterday.
recurring_note: ↑ Day 4 — 3.3k stars; v0.1.6 adds Mochi desktop overlay

name: ReelMimic
hook: Show it a video you love, get a new video in the same style. An AI crew (Claude Code or Codex) plans, builds, and reviews it with you: agents run in parallel on different shots, a separate reviewer agent checks each one and triggers fixes when something's wrong. Supports watercolor, crayon, and custom style extraction. A 30–60 second video takes 1–3.5 hours depending on style. Trending #8 in GitHub's global daily trending repos on October 4. 1.2k stars.

name: jevgrep
hook: A CLI for coding agents that finds code by asking what it does rather than what it says — returns relevant files, reading leads, and verbatim source excerpts in response to plain English like 'where is JWT validation?' The creator (David Zhang) verified a 40% agent cost reduction on SWE-bench by feeding only the relevant files instead of the full repo. IndyDevDan dedicated a video to Jev-based context engineering this week. 2.1k stars.

name: ECC
hook: The agent harness OS sitting at #1 on GitHub's claude-code topic with 272k stars. ECC wraps Claude Code (and Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and 8 others) with a complete software-development lifecycle: 293 reusable skills covering TDD, security, frontend/backend, and domain work; 68 specialized agents for planning, architecture, build repair, and code review; 94 workflow commands; AgentShield security scanning for prompts, config, and permissions; and session-persistent memory. v2.2.3 shipped in October 2026. The ethos: plan → test → implement → review → verify → remember → improve.

name: Graphify
hook: Type `/graphify .` in Claude Code and it transforms your entire codebase — plus docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs — into a queryable knowledge graph in seconds. Local deterministic AST parsing via tree-sitter (37 languages, no LLM call) handles code; semantic analysis handles docs. Outputs graph.html (interactive click-through visualization), GRAPH_REPORT.md (key concepts and surprising connections), and graph.json (queryable data). An MCP server mode enables repeated programmatic access. Community detection uses the Leiden algorithm. 123.4k stars.
install: uv tool install graphifyy && graphify install

name: agent-skills (Addy Osmani)
hook: Production-grade engineering skills by Addy Osmani (Google Chrome DevTools lead, 'Learning Patterns' author). 25 skills that encode the discipline separating production code from prototypes — Google's engineering culture baked in: Hyrum's Law, the test pyramid, trunk-based development, and Zero Tolerance Flakiness for tests. Nine lifecycle slash commands (/spec, /plan, /build, /test, /review, /security-audit, /perf-audit, /ship, /skills) map to the full development lifecycle. 101k stars.

name: Karpathy Guidelines Skill
hook: When Andrej Karpathy posted his frustrations with AI coding agents in January 2026, it went viral instantly. Forrest Chang turned the thread into four hard behavioral rules: think before coding, make surgical changes, surface assumptions and tradeoffs, define verifiable success criteria. Now the most-starred Claude Code behavioral skill on GitHub at 210k stars, with 35.1k installs on the skills.sh registry. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode, Copilot, and any AGENTS.md-compatible agent.

name: gstack (Garry Tan)
hook: Y Combinator's CEO open-sourced his personal Claude Code configuration on March 12, 2026 — it hit 33k stars in week one. Now at 135k stars. Ships 23 specialist roles (CEO, designer, engineering manager, QA lead, release engineer, and 18 more) as slash commands plus 8 power tools. Work moves through a fixed loop: Think → Plan → Build → Review → Test → Ship → Reflect. Tan averaged 10,000 lines of code and 100 pull requests per week over a 50-day sprint using it. Works with Claude Code and 7 other agents.

name: Universal Modder
hook: Point Claude at any game you own and it mods it. Skills, CLI, and fal MCP server cover 12 engine playbooks — Unity, Unreal, Godot, Source, Bethesda, Minecraft, .NET/XNA (Terraria, Stardew, Celeste), RE Engine, and more. Claude runs a 10-step loop: recon, reverse-engineer, set up a safe lab, read game code, build one working slice, generate art/3D/SFX/music via fal, test in-game, record, package, document. Sprites, seamless textures, 3D objects, full SFX tracks, and cutscene video all from a text prompt. 2.8k stars; #2 in GitHub's global daily trending repos on October 4.
